messages:
Ravi P.: Quick announcement: next quarter were standardizing webhook auth for Jira and moving all CI pipelines to tokenless runner credentials using our new OIDC broker. This affects any service that ingests Jira webhooks or stores org-scoped CI tokens.

Lina M.: Can you clarify scope? Is this org-level only or repo-level too?

Ravi P.: Both. Were enforcing signed webhook secrets + JWT validation at the ingress layer and replacing long-lived CI tokens with ephemeral OIDC tokens minted by `rw-oidc-broker`. Timeline: pilot week starts 2026-05-04, gradual opt-in May 11-25, org enforcement May 26.

Tom S.: Will this break our existing terraform-managed webhook endpoints?

Ravi P.: No immediate break. Well add a compatibility header that the ingress will accept for 2 weeks after enforcement. But please update your terraform to provision the new `jira.webhook_secret` resource. See docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/platform/jira-webhooks#auth-migration.

Maya (sec): Security note: all previous webhook shared secrets will be rotated automatically for managed vendor integrations. For self-managed endpoints you must rotate by May 20 or they will stop delivering.

Eve Q.: How do I test locally?

Ravi P.: Use the test harness:```bash
# start local ingress with jwt verification
make run-local-ingress
# sign a webhook
python scripts/sign_webhook.py --payload event.json --secret $LOCAL_SECRET > signed.json
# post
curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @signed.json http://localhost:8080/jira/webhook
```

Lina M.: OIDC broker: any changes for self-hosted runners?

Ravi P.: Self-hosted runners will obtain ephemeral credentials from the broker by presenting the runner identity. The broker integrates with our IDP (SAML / OIDC). You will need to install the `rw-oidc-agent` on any runner host and update runner config like:```yaml
runner:
  oidc: true
  oidc_agent_url: http://127.0.0.1:9200
```

CI-bot: Reminder: migration checklist added to repo `infra/ci-migrations` 1 files to review.

Tom S.: What about third-party apps (PagerDuty, Linear) that consume Jira webhooks?

Maya (sec): For vendor destinations we will spin up proxy adapters where feasible. Vendors that support webhook signing will get instructions. If a vendor cannot be upgraded, open an exception ticket with product and security justification. Exceptions expire after 30 days.

Eve Q.: Is there a migration CLI?

Ravi P.: Yes: `rw-webhook-migrate` and `rw-oidc-attach`. Example:```bash
# rotate webhook secret and register JWT public key
rw-webhook-migrate --project product-analytics --from-secret $OLD --to-secret $NEW --register-key ./pubkey.pem
# attach oidc to a runner
rw-oidc-attach --runner-id runner-43 --agent-url http://oidc-agent:9200
```

Lina M.: Do you have a rollback path if webhooks start failing?

Ravi P.: Well keep ingress in permissive mode for 48 hours after each rollout batch where it logs verification failures but still accepts requests. If needed we can flip back to legacy auth for specific endpoints via feature flag.

Infra-bot: Scheduled scan: inventory webhook endpoints May 1-3. Teams: update the `webhook_owner` field in your service manifest before May 3.

Tom S.: Any changes to logging or observability for failed signature verification?

Ravi P.: Yes. New metrics: `webhook.signature.failures` and `oidc.token.requests` (per-repo label). Dashboards: Platform -> Webhooks -> Auth. Alerting: >10 failures/min for any single endpoint triggers a P2.

Maya (sec): Also enforcing HSTS and strict TLS for all webhook endpoints. If your endpoint uses non-ACME certs, file a migration ticket.

Eve Q.: For repo owners: do we need to update GitHub app perms?

Ravi P.: No change to GitHub app perms required for this migration, but were encouraging teams to move to repo-scoped apps where possible.

Lina M.: How do we sign up for pilot?

Ravi P.: Fill the pilot form: https://go.redwood.dev/jira-webhook-pilot by Apr 28. Pilot slots limited; we'll prioritize customer-facing and high-traffic services.

Tom S.: Thanks. We'll register `ingress` and `webhook-proxy`.

Ravi P.: Awesome. I'll post a follow-up with the exact rollout batch assignments and a short how-to video. If you need an exception, ping Maya and include use case + delivery IDs. :white_check_mark:
